title: Strassen's algorithm, inversion in O(M(n)) and nested dissection with fast matrix multiplication, in Lean 4
abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization, in the arithmetic cost model, of fast matrix multiplication and its use in Gaussian elimination. Algorithms are written in a writer monad that charges one unit for every addition, subtraction, negation, multiplication and inversion performed through its primitives; costs are statements about these explicit algorithms, whose definitions are part of the statements. A matrix multiplication algorithm is a counted procedure together with proofs that it computes the product and performs at most M(n) operations on n x n matrices, M monotone. Six theorems are compared: (1) over every ring, Strassen's algorithm on matrices of size 2^k computes the product with exactly 7^k multiplications and 6(7^k - 4^k) additive operations; (2) 2 < log2(7) < 3, and over every ring Strassen's algorithm padded with zeros to the next power of two is a multiplication algorithm with at most 49 n^(log2 7) operations for n >= 1, whose bound satisfies 4 M(2^k) <= M(2^(k+1)) and 1 <= M(1); (3) over a field, for every multiplication algorithm whose bound satisfies these two conditions, block inversion of diag(A, 1) padded to size 2^ceil(log2 n) returns the inverse and the determinant of an n x n matrix A whose leading principal minors are all nonzero, and performs fewer than 5 M(2^ceil(log2 n)) operations (at most 5 C 2^omega n^omega when n >= 1, omega >= 0 and M(m) <= C m^omega for all m >= 1); (4)-(6) for every field K, every multiplication algorithm over K with M(m) <= C m^omega for m >= 1, omega > 2, satisfying the two conditions above, and every plane graph (respectively the square of a plane graph of maximum degree at most D) on n vertices, there is a separator tree covering all vertices such that block elimination along it computes the determinant of every matrix over K whose off-diagonal nonzero entries are edges of that graph, provided the elimination meets only invertible blocks (theorem (6): no such hypothesis for positive definite matrices, on squares of plane graphs, over a field with a partial order and a star structure satisfying IsOrderedRing, PosMulReflectLT and StarRing, such as the real numbers), with at most (5 C 2^omega + 2C + 2)(2T + 1)^omega / (1 - (2/3)^(omega/2 - 1)) n^(omega/2) operations, T = 50000, respectively T = 40 (1062 (D + 1)^2 + 1). Plane graphs are rotation systems of connected Mathlib simple graphs satisfying Euler's formula, so they have at least one edge (faces are cycles of darts, and the one-vertex graph has none). The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
